N1_guard_not_wired_into_create._note: The pre-fix state of create: the helper exists, nothing calls it. Reddens create's two refusal axes and leaves set-property's (V4/V9) green — the pair with the set-property spec is what proves each call site is locked independently. ⛤ Anchor re-pinned after the review fix: the call is now multi-line and returns the resolutions create reuses, so the mutant substitutes an empty result instead of deleting the line — type-preserving. ⛤ The set grew with the review fixes: V10/V11/V12/V14 also ride the create call site, so removing it (or emptying the predicate) kills the refusal on all of them at once. That is arithmetic, not scope creep — N4/N10/N11 are what separate the individual guarantees.

N4_guard_skipped_under_dry_run._note: Type-preserving one-line wrap — the shape that made the T6 guard's ordering unlocked until an axis existed for it. Reddens ONLY V3: V1 runs without --dry-run and still refuses, which is precisely why the dry-run clause needs its own axis.
